derivation: Foundation 52 Media.Video, read from the pinned Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Video.dll. It is `.class public auto ansi sealed beforefieldinit` extending System.Object over seven private fields -- filename, duration, width, height, framesPerSecond, graphicsDevice and soundtrackType -- with five public get-only properties, each one ldfld, and two `assembly` getters, get_GraphicsDevice and get_Filename, which are not identities. The single constructor is `assembly` and stores all seven arguments with no validation; the one conversion it performs is duration, which arrives as an Int32 and is stored as `new TimeSpan(0, 0, 0, 0, duration)` -- the five-argument form whose last parameter is milliseconds. The constructor's first argument is a Graphics.GraphicsDevice, which it stores and calls no member of, which is why naming a partial type here was never a blocker under the Foundation 40 rule.
